model_organism.citation: Loss of hepatic DRP1 exacerbates alcoholic hepatitis by inducing megamitochondria and mitochondrial maladaptation (PMID: 35698731)
phenotypes: Liver-specific Drp1 KO (L-DRP1 KO) mice had increased megamitochondria
Increased liver injury and inflammation, further exacerbated by chronic-plus-binge alcohol feeding
Attenuated alcohol-induced increases in mitochondrial oxygen consumption, hepatic NAD+, acylcarnitine and ketones, indicating metabolic maladaptation
Increased cGAS-STING-interferon pathway gene expression regardless of alcohol
Increased cytosolic mtDNA and mitochondrial dysfunction with alcohol
Loss of Drp1 (DNM1L) in postmitotic neurons (cre-loxP) caused increased mitochondrial oxidative damage
Accumulation of LC3, SQSTM1/p62 and ubiquitin on division-defective mitochondria, suggesting decreased mitochondrial turnover

model_organism.citation: Mitochondrial dynamics and quality control regulate proteostasis in neuronal ischemia-reperfusion (PMID: 40016670)
phenotypes: Neuronal mitochondrial proteostasis response to in vitro ischemia-reperfusion (OGD/R) was influenced by fusion and fission machinery, including DNM1L/DRP1 cKO in neurons

model_organism.citation: Peroxisomes control mitochondrial dynamics and the mitochondrion-dependent apoptosis pathway (PMID: 31076512)
phenotypes: In Pex3- or Pex5-knockout MEFs, mitochondrial fragmentation was dependent on Drp1 (DNM1L)
Peroxisome deficiency increased cytosolic cytochrome c and caspase activity and enhanced etoposide-induced apoptosis

biological.citation: Drp1 splice variants regulate ovarian cancer mitochondrial dynamics and tumor progression (PMID: 39191946)
biological.summary: The Drp1 (DNM1L) splice variant lacking exon 16 localizes to microtubules and associates less with mitochondrial fission sites. This produces fused mitochondrial networks, enhanced respiration, pro-tumorigenic phenotypes, impaired fission in response to apoptotic stimuli, and reduced chemosensitivity. High expression of this variant relative to other transcripts predicts poor outcome in ovarian cancer patients, and variant-specific siRNAs reverse the effects.

biological.citation: Obesity causes mitochondrial fragmentation and dysfunction in white adipocytes due to RalA activation (PMID: 38286821)
biological.summary: RalA activation in white adipocytes after high-fat diet reverses the inhibitory Ser637 phosphorylation of Drp1, increasing fission and mitochondrial fragmentation. Adipose tissue DNM1L expression correlates positively with obesity and insulin resistance in humans.

biological.citation: Aberrant mitochondrial morphology and function associated with impaired mitophagy and DNM1L-MAPK/ERK signaling in aged LRRK2(R1441G) mice (PMID: 33300446)
biological.summary: DNM1L/Drp1 knockdown in MEFs slowed mitochondrial clearance, so DNM1L is required for mitophagy, and it disrupted the mitochondrial network. FCCP-induced DNM1L-Ser616 and ERK phosphorylation occurred in WT but not LRRK2 R1441G mutant MEFs, despite similar total DNM1L levels, indicating impaired DNM1L activation in the mutant.

biological.citation: ERK1/2-mediated activation of DRP1 regulates mitochondrial dynamics and apoptosis in chondrocytes (PMID: 34767958)
biological.summary: DRP1 expression is elevated in human OA cartilage and in mouse DMM joints. IL-1β induces DRP1 expression and activity through ERK1/2, causing mitochondrial fragmentation and Bax-mediated cytochrome c release with apoptosis. Mdivi-1 or ERK1/2 inhibition blocks these effects.

biological.citation: Targeting DNM1L/DRP1-FIS1 axis inhibits high-grade glioma progression by impeding mitochondrial respiratory cristae remodeling (PMID: 39350223)
biological.summary: DNM1L/DRP1 positively regulates FIS1, while MFF competitively inhibits FIS1 interaction. DNM1L/DRP1-FIS1 axis knockdown impaired mitophagy, cristae remodeling and OXPHOS, and reduced proliferation and xenograft growth of glioma cells and stem cells.
biological.sample_size: 54 resected glioma patients; 7141 mitochondria analyzed by TEM

biological.citation: Cancer-associated SNRPD3 mutation confers resistance to hypoxia, which is attenuated by DRP1 inhibition (PMID: 38241813)
biological.summary: The SNRPD3 G96V spliceosome mutation causes differential splicing of DNM1L mRNA under hypoxia and excessive mitochondrial fragmentation. The DRP1 inhibitor Mdivi-1 restores mitochondrial morphology and attenuates hypoxia resistance.

biological.citation: Loss of hepatic DRP1 exacerbates alcoholic hepatitis by inducing megamitochondria and mitochondrial maladaptation (PMID: 35698731)
biological.summary: Hepatic DRP1 is decreased in human alcoholic hepatitis and in alcohol-fed mice, because alcohol impairs TFEB-mediated induction of DNM1L. Liver-specific DRP1 knockout causes megamitochondria, reduced mitophagy, cytosolic mtDNA and cGAS-STING-interferon activation, with increased liver injury and inflammation.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Missense mutations in the middle domain of DNM1L cause infantile encephalopathy in humans and peroxisomal and mitochondrial defects in Drosophila and humans
biological.summary: Human wild-type DNM1L rescues Drosophila drp1 mutants. The p.G350R and p.A395D middle-domain variants instead produce aggregated mitochondria with trafficking defects in fly neurons, supporting their pathogenicity in patients with encephalopathy.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - DNM1L-related mitochondrial fission defect presenting as spastic paraparesis and optic atrophy
biological.summary: A de novo heterozygous DNM1L p.Thr59Ile variant in the GTPase domain was found in a patient with spastic paraparesis, cerebellar syndrome and optic atrophy. Patient myoblasts showed mega-mitochondria along an elongated mitochondrial network, and muscle biopsy showed mild CI+III and COX defects.

biological.citation: Reversibility and therapeutic feasibility of DNM1L-associated neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41786974)
biological.summary: Expressing DNM1L variants in developing mouse brain caused severe neuronal loss at the early postnatal stage. In a human stem-cell model with chemogenetic control of DNM1L, over 75% of the pathological transcriptional changes were reversible even in differentiated neurons. Targeting mitochondrial biogenesis prevented neurodegeneration.
